What's Included

Your Automated Mode package includes:

  • Browser Extension - The main automation tool (folder: VEO Extension)
  • N8N Workflow - The polling workflow file (veo-polling-workflow.json)
  • This User Guide - Step-by-step instructions
  • CSV Template - For importing prompts (optional)
Automated Mode means the extension automatically polls your N8N workflow for new tasks. N8N reads from Baserow, sends tasks to the extension, and saves results back - fully automated!

1. Install the Browser Extension

Use Opera or Opera GX instead of Chrome! Chrome sometimes causes problems with the extension. For best results, use OperaGX or Opera.
  1. Unzip the downloaded file. Move the extracted folder to a convenient location (e.g. your Desktop). The folder should be named VEO Extension.
    Important: Do NOT rename or move this folder after installing the extension. The browser needs this folder to stay in the same place!
  2. Open Opera (recommended) and go to: opera://extensions/
    (or Chrome: chrome://extensions/)
  3. Enable "Developer mode" in the top-right corner
  4. Click "Load unpacked"
  5. Select the VEO Extension folder
  6. The VEO icon should appear in your toolbar. If you don't see it, click the puzzle/extensions icon and pin it.

The VEO extension should appear in your extensions menu. Click the pin icon to keep it visible in your toolbar.

2. Create Baserow Table

  1. Create a free account at baserow.io
  2. After logging in, click "Create new" and then "Database"
  3. In the left sidebar, click "+ New table" to create a new table:
  4. In the dialog that appears, select "Import a CSV file" and upload the included Baserow CSV Template.csv from your package. Then click "Add table":
  5. Now you need to change the Field Types. After the CSV import, all fields are plain text. You need to change some of them to the correct type.

    How to change a field type: Click the small arrow next to the field name, then click "Edit field":
    Change these fields:
    • ID → Change type to Autonumber
    • VEO Prompt → Change type to Long Text
    • Image URL → Change type to Long Text
    • Image Prompt → Change type to Long Text
    • Imagegen Reference → Change type to Long Text
    • Video_URL → Change type to Long Text
    • Start Frame → Change type to Long Text
    • End Frame → Change type to Long Text
    • Status → Change type to Single Select, then click "+ Add an option" to add these 4 options: pending, processing, completed, failed (colors don't matter)
    • Mode → Change type to Single Select, then add these options: text, image, frames, Imagegen

All Fields Overview

Field Name (EXACT!) Field Type Description
ID Autonumber Auto-generated row number
VEO Prompt Long Text Your video prompt (used in modes: text, image, frames)
Image URL Long Text Reference image URL (used in mode: image)
Image Prompt Long Text Image generation prompt (used in mode: Imagegen)
Imagegen Reference Long Text Optional reference image for image generation (used in mode: Imagegen)
Video_URL Long Text Filled automatically by the extension (both Images and Videos get saved here)
Status Single Select Options: pending, processing, completed, failed
Mode Single Select Options: text, image, frames, Imagegen
Start Frame Long Text Start frame image URL (used in mode: frames)
End Frame Long Text End frame image URL (used in mode: frames)
If you see any other fields after the import, just delete them and keep only the fields shown above.
Column names must be 100% identical!
  • Case matters: VEO Prompt ≠ veo prompt
  • Spaces matter: Image URL ≠ ImageURL
  • Tip: Copy field names directly from this guide to avoid typos!

3. How to Prepare Your Baserow Table for Generations

Before starting the automation, you need to fill your Baserow table with tasks. Here's how the different generation modes work and which fields to fill.

Required for EVERY row, regardless of mode: The fields Mode and Status must always be filled. Set Status to pending and Mode to the generation mode you want. The ID field is filled automatically.

Generation Modes

Mode What it does Fields to fill
text Creates a VEO video from text prompt only VEO Prompt
image Creates a VEO video using text prompt + 1 or more reference images VEO Prompt + Image URL
For multiple reference images, separate URLs with a comma: URL1,URL2
frames Creates a VEO video from start & end frame images VEO Prompt + Start Frame (required) + End Frame (optional)
Imagegen Creates an IMAGE (not video!) using Google's Nano Banana Pro Image Prompt + Imagegen Reference (optional)
For Imagegen mode: Use the Image Prompt field, NOT VEO Prompt! The VEO Prompt field stays empty for image generation.

Here is an example of how it could look like using all the different modes:

How to Turn Your Reference Images into Links

For the modes image, frames, and Imagegen, you need to provide image URLs. If your images are on your computer, you need to upload them to get a link first.

Use image2url.com to upload your images and get direct URLs. Simply upload your image and copy the generated URL into the corresponding Baserow field.

The URLs from image2url.com are permanent and work directly with the extension. They look like: https://img.image2url.com/abc123.jpg

Advanced: Automate Reference Images with N8N

If you're already experienced with N8N, you can take this a step further. Instead of manually uploading images and copying URLs, you can build a workflow that generates images and retrieves the URLs automatically.

You can also fully automate the process of populating your Baserow table - from generating prompts to filling in all the fields - by building a custom N8N workflow for it. The possibilities are endless once you combine the extension with your own N8N automations!

4. Import N8N Workflow

Now we set up the N8N workflow that connects your Baserow table with the extension.

  1. Open your N8N instance (self-hosted or cloud)
  2. Create a new workflow
  3. Click the three dots (...) in the top-right corner of the workflow editor
  4. Select "Import from File...":
  5. Select the included veo-polling-workflow.json from your package

Verify the Workflow

After importing, check that every node is connected and the workflow looks like this:

The workflow consists of these nodes:

The workflow has 4 main sections:

PROMPT + IMAGE REFERENCE (red section)

  • Webhook1 → receives all requests from the extension (task requests, results, failures, retries)
  • If3 → routes the request to the correct section based on message type
  • Get many rows1 → fetches pending tasks from Baserow
  • Parser1 → selects the highest-priority task
  • If4 → checks if a valid task was found
  • Update Status to processing1 → marks the task as "processing" in Baserow
  • Code in JavaScript2 → prepares the task data for the extension
  • Respond to Webhook3 / Respond to Webhook4 → sends the task back or responds with empty if no tasks

SAVE GENERATED VEO VIDEOS (green section)

  • Result Parser1 → processes completed results from the extension
  • Has Media? → checks if media files were included in the result
  • Upload a file1 → uploads the generated video/image to MinIO S3 storage
  • Set MinIO URL1 → constructs the permanent download URL
  • Update Video_URL1 → saves the MinIO URL and marks the row as "completed" in Baserow
  • Respond to Webhook6 → acknowledges the result
  • Mark Failed (no media) → if no media was received, marks the row as "failed"
  • Respond Failed → acknowledges the failed result

HANDLE TASK FAILED (purple section)

  • Is TaskFailed? → checks if the extension reported a task failure
  • Parse Failed Task → extracts the row ID from the failure report
  • Update Status to failed → marks the row as "failed" in Baserow
  • Respond Task Failed → acknowledges the failure

RETRY FAILED + STUCK ROWS (blue section)

  • Is RetryFailed? → checks if the extension is requesting a retry scan
  • Get ALL rows → fetches all rows from the Baserow table
  • Find Failed/Stuck Rows → scans for rows stuck on "processing" or "failed"
  • All Completed? → checks if there are any stuck rows left
  • Reset to Pending → resets the first stuck row back to "pending" for retry
  • Respond Retry Info → tells the extension how many rows need retry
  • Respond All Done → tells the extension all tasks are completed
Make sure every node is connected! If you see any disconnected nodes, drag a connection line from the output of one node to the input of the next one according to the image above.
Don't change the workflow structure! All nodes are already connected and configured with the correct logic. You only need to set up the Baserow credentials and field IDs in the next step.

5. Configure Workflow & Connect to Baserow

Now we connect the workflow to your Baserow table and set up the webhook. You need to configure all Baserow nodes (select your database and table) and the S3/MinIO upload node (your storage credentials). The JavaScript code nodes are pre-configured and don't need changes.

Overview: There are 7 Baserow nodes and 1 S3 upload node that need your credentials. All other nodes (Code, If, Respond to Webhook) are already configured and should not be changed.

Step 1: Create Baserow Credentials

First, we need to tell N8N how to access your Baserow account. Click on any Baserow node in the workflow (e.g. "Get many rows1") and click the pencil icon next to "Credential to connect with".

A credential form will open. Fill in the following:

  • Email: Enter the email you use to log into Baserow
  • Password: Enter your normal Baserow login password
  • Host: Leave as https://api.baserow.io (default)
N8N will automatically handle the API authentication in the background using your login credentials. You do not need to create a separate API token in Baserow for N8N.

Click "Save". This credential will be reused across all Baserow nodes.

Step 2: Configure "Webhook1"

Double-click the "Webhook1" node. This is the entry point for all communication between the extension and N8N:

  • HTTP Method: POST
  • Path: Enter your desired URL ending (e.g. Veo-pollingkpdh). Choose something unique so it's hard to guess.
  • Authentication: None
  • Respond: Using 'Respond to Webhook' Node
Important: Copy the Production URL shown at the top of the Webhook node — NOT the Test URL! The Production URL is only available after you activate the workflow. Click the "Active" toggle in the top-right corner first.

Step 3: Configure "Get many rows1"

Double-click the "Get many rows1" node. This fetches pending tasks from your Baserow table:

  • Credential to connect with: Select the Baserow credential you created
  • Resource: Row
  • Operation: Get Many
  • Database Name or ID: Select your database
  • Table Name or ID: Select your table
  • Return All: Off
  • Limit: 1
  • Under Options → Filters:
    • Field Name or ID: Status
    • Filter: Contains
    • Value: pending

Step 4: Configure "Update Status to processing1"

Double-click the "Update Status to processing1" node:

  • Credential to connect with: Select the same Baserow credential
  • Resource: Row
  • Operation: Update
  • Database Name or ID: Select your database
  • Table Name or ID: Select your table
  • Row ID: {{ $json.id }}
  • Data to Send: Define Below for Each Column
  • Under Fields to Send:
    • Field Name or ID: Status
    • Field Value: processing

Step 5: Configure "Upload a file1" (S3/MinIO Storage)

This node uploads the generated videos/images to your S3-compatible storage (MinIO, AWS S3, DigitalOcean Spaces, etc.). Double-click it:

  • Credential to connect with: Create or select your S3 credential (click the pencil icon). Enter your S3 Access Key, Secret Key, and endpoint URL.
  • Resource: File
  • Operation: Upload
  • Bucket Name: Your bucket name (e.g. my-videos)
  • File Name: VEO/{{ $json.filename }}
  • Binary File: On (enabled)
  • Input Binary Field: data
S3/MinIO Setup: If you don't have S3 storage yet, you can use MinIO (free, self-hosted) or any S3-compatible service. The extension sends the generated media as base64 to N8N, which then uploads it to your storage for permanent URLs.

Step 6: Configure "Set MinIO URL1"

This code node constructs the permanent download URL for each generated file. It combines your MinIO/S3 server address with the filename. Double-click it:

You need to edit the JavaScript code inside this node. Replace the placeholder URL with your own MinIO/S3 URL:

const resultParser = $('Result Parser1').first().json;
const minioUrl = `http://YOUR_MINIO_IP:9000/YOUR_BUCKET/VEO/${resultParser.filename}`;
return [{ json: { rowId: resultParser.rowId, resultUrl: minioUrl } }];

Change these two things:

  • YOUR_MINIO_IP:9000 → Replace with your MinIO/S3 server address and port (e.g. 123.45.67.89:9000 or s3.amazonaws.com)
  • YOUR_BUCKET → Replace with your bucket name (e.g. my-videos)

Example: If your MinIO is at 45.67.89.123:9000 and your bucket is called my-videos, the line should look like:

const minioUrl = `http://45.67.89.123:9000/my-videos/VEO/${resultParser.filename}`;
Important: Your S3/MinIO bucket must be set to public (public read access). Otherwise the download URLs won't work. In MinIO, you can set this under Buckets → your bucket → Access Policy → public.
Tip: The URL format must match exactly how your files are accessible from the browser. Test by opening http://YOUR_MINIO_IP:9000/YOUR_BUCKET/ in your browser — you should see the bucket contents.

Step 7: Configure "Update Video_URL1"

This node saves the permanent storage URL back to Baserow and marks the row as completed. Double-click it:

  • Credential to connect with: Select the same Baserow credential
  • Resource: Row
  • Operation: Update
  • Database Name or ID: Select your database
  • Table Name or ID: Select your table
  • Row ID: {{ $json.rowId }}
  • Data to Send: Define Below for Each Column
  • Under Fields to Send (two fields):
    • Field 1: Field Name or ID: Video_URL — Field Value: {{ $json.resultUrl }}
    • Field 2: Field Name or ID: Status — Field Value: completed

Step 8: Configure "Mark Failed (no media)"

This node marks a row as "failed" when the extension completed the task but no media was received (e.g. content policy violation). Double-click it:

  • Credential to connect with: Select the same Baserow credential
  • Resource: Row
  • Operation: Update
  • Database Name or ID: Select your database
  • Table Name or ID: Select your table
  • Row ID: {{ $json.rowId }}
  • Data to Send: Define Below for Each Column
  • Under Fields to Send:
    • Field Name or ID: Status
    • Field Value: failed

Step 9: Configure "Update Status to failed"

This node is in the HANDLE TASK FAILED section (purple). It marks a row as "failed" when the extension reports a generation failure. Double-click it:

  • Credential to connect with: Select the same Baserow credential
  • Resource: Row
  • Operation: Update
  • Database Name or ID: Select your database
  • Table Name or ID: Select your table
  • Row ID: {{ $json.rowId }}
  • Data to Send: Define Below for Each Column
  • Under Fields to Send:
    • Field Name or ID: Status
    • Field Value: failed

Step 10: Configure "Get ALL rows"

This node is in the RETRY FAILED + STUCK ROWS section (blue). After all tasks are processed, the extension triggers a retry scan. This node fetches all rows to find any stuck ones. Double-click it:

  • Credential to connect with: Select the same Baserow credential
  • Resource: Row
  • Operation: Get Many
  • Database Name or ID: Select your database
  • Table Name or ID: Select your table
  • Return All: On (enabled — this must be on to scan all rows!)
Return All must be ON! Unlike "Get many rows1" which only fetches 1 pending row, this node needs to fetch ALL rows to find any failed or stuck ones.

Step 11: Configure "Reset to Pending"

This node resets a failed/stuck row back to "pending" so the extension can retry it. Double-click it:

  • Credential to connect with: Select the same Baserow credential
  • Resource: Row
  • Operation: Update
  • Database Name or ID: Select your database
  • Table Name or ID: Select your table
  • Row ID: {{ $json.rowId }}
  • Data to Send: Define Below for Each Column
  • Under Fields to Send:
    • Field Name or ID: Status
    • Field Value: pending
Important: Make sure you select the correct Baserow credential in ALL Baserow nodes. If any node shows a red warning icon, click it and re-select your credential. All 7 Baserow nodes must use the same credential with the same database and table selected.

Step 12: Enter the Webhook URL in the Extension

Now that all nodes are configured, activate the workflow by clicking the toggle in the top-right corner of N8N. Then go back to the Webhook1 node and copy the Production URL.

Open the VEO Extension in your browser toolbar. Under "Webhook Settings", paste the same Production URL into both fields:

  • Poll URL (Fetch Tasks)
  • Result URL (Send Results)

Then click "Save URLs".

Both URLs must be the same! The extension uses the same webhook endpoint for all communication (requesting tasks, sending results, reporting failures, and triggering retry scans).

Start the Automation

Now, if you got your table filled, you can start generating:

  1. Make sure Google Flow is open in at least one browser tab (labs.google/fx)
  2. Toggle the main switch to ON
  3. The extension will now automatically:
    • Poll N8N for pending tasks
    • Generate videos/images via API (up to 5 tasks in parallel)
    • Send the results back to N8N
    • N8N uploads to S3/MinIO and saves the permanent URL to Baserow
    • After all tasks are done, automatically retry any failed/stuck rows
That's it! The automation is now running. The extension will keep polling for new tasks until you turn it off.
Adding more tasks: Simply add new rows to your Baserow table with Status = pending. The extension will automatically pick them up on the next poll cycle — no need to restart anything!

6. Before & During Generating

Before You Start

Make sure you have Google Flow open in at least one browser tab: go to labs.google/fx and make sure you're logged in.

It's recommended to open a new Flow project before you start generating. Click "+ New project". This keeps your workspace clean.

Why don't I see any generations on the Flow page?
This is completely normal! The extension works via direct API calls, so you will NOT see any visual activity on the Flow page. The tab just needs to be open in the background — the extension handles everything automatically behind the scenes. As long as the extension shows progress, everything is working correctly.

After every session (when the extension finishes or you want to stop), always click Clear & Stop as well as Clear History in the extension to make sure everything works fine the next time you start it again.

During Generating

The extension works via API calls, so you can freely use other tabs and windows while it's running. Just make sure to keep the Flow tab open (don't close it) and don't close your browser.

If You Encounter Errors

  1. Click Clear & Stop and Clear History in the extension
  2. Close the extension popup
  3. In Baserow, set the error rows (they will show "processing" or "failed") back to pending
  4. Open the extension again and start the automation
  5. You can simply continue from where you left off - the completed rows will be ignored since they are already finished
Automatic Retry: The extension automatically retries failed/stuck rows after all tasks are processed. You usually don't need to manually reset rows — the retry system handles it for you!
N8N Payload Size: When using video upscaling (especially 4K), generated files can be 15-25MB. If uploads fail silently, increase the N8N_PAYLOAD_SIZE_MAX environment variable in your N8N Docker Compose or .env file:
N8N_PAYLOAD_SIZE_MAX=100
If you can't resolve an error, contact me through the email on page 1: [email protected]

7. Outputs per Generation (Multi-Output)

By default, the extension generates 1 output per task. You can increase this to generate up to 4 outputs per task.

How to Set Output Count

  1. Click the VEO Extension icon in your toolbar
  2. In the Automated tab, you'll see "Outputs per Generation" with buttons 1-4
  3. Click the number you want (e.g. 3 for 3 outputs per task)
  4. This setting is saved and applies to all future tasks until you change it
How it works: When set to e.g. 3 outputs, the extension tells Google Flow to generate 3 results for each prompt. All result URLs are saved together in the Video_URL field, separated by commas.

What Happens with Errors?

If you set outputs to 3 but only 2 succeed and 1 fails:

  • The extension saves the 2 successful results (partial success)
  • The task is marked as completed, not retried
  • Only if ALL outputs fail, the extension retries the task (up to 3 times)

Multi-Output Downloads

When a task has multiple outputs, the Video_URL field contains comma-separated URLs. If you download from Baserow, each URL is separated by a comma.

8. Troubleshooting

If stuck: Disable the extension in your browser's extension settings, re-enable it, refresh the Google Flow page, and reconnect.

Common Issues

Problem Solution
Extension doesn't poll for tasks Check that your webhook URLs are correct and the N8N workflow is Active. Make sure you're using the Production URL, not the Test URL.
N8N shows red errors Open the failed execution in N8N. Most likely a Baserow credential or field ID is incorrect. Re-check your node configuration.
Tasks stay "processing" forever The extension may have encountered an error. Click Clear & Stop, reset the row to pending in Baserow, and restart.
Video_URL is empty after completion Check the "Update Video_URL" node in N8N. Make sure the field mapping is correct and the credential is selected.

How to Get Error Logs (for Support)

If you need help, send us the extension's error logs:

  1. Press CTRL + Shift + I to open Developer Tools
  2. Click on the Console tab
  3. Copy all log messages (lines starting with [VEO])
  4. Also check your N8N execution history for any failed executions
  5. Send the logs via email to [email protected]
